subject: Commercial path & approver roster for Redwood trial
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@clarityretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@clarityretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial path & approver roster for Redwood trial

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great talk today — thanks for walking through the scope. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement readiness and the commercial path. TL;DR: two viable paths (card-start vs PO/contract), need to confirm budget owner + legal timeline.

Post-call summary:
- Pilot scope: 3 models, 10k inference units/day, 30-day trial window.
- Success criteria: sub-150ms p95, under $0.003/token cost target on average.
- Data handling: no persistent storage of raw customer PII; will sign the data processing annex.

Questions we flagged for procurement thread:
1) Paper process: do you require a signed contract + SOW for proof-of-concept, or is a PO sufficient?
2) Payment method: PO (net-30) vs corporate card for immediate start — which does procurement prefer?
3) Marketplace: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace (makes procurement + billing simpler) or direct invoicing?
4) Budget / signatory: who owns the budget and who will sign the purchase (economic buyer, finance sponsor, contract signatory)?

Attachments for your review: Redwood-trial-quote.pdf (quote + line items), procurement-checklist.xlsx (internal procurement questions).

Proposed quick options:
A) Card-first: start within 48 hours, small committed spend, no SOW required, then convert to PO later.
B) PO + SOW: 2–3 week lead time (contracts + legal review), pilot begins after signed SOW.

Next asks from you: please confirm preferred payment path (card vs PO), primary budget owner (name & email), and an estimated legal/contract review window.

I’ll loop Marissa for procurement support and Ben for pricing exceptions if needed.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@clarityretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clarityretail.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial path & approver roster for Redwood trial

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:

- Payment method: Procurement prefers a PO / net-30 for pilots > $20k, but we can do a corporate card for an initial smoke test if you can split the cost into a smaller invoice.
- Marketplace: we prefer AWS Marketplace where available (easier for our procurement, but we need Redwood to publish the offer).
- Budget owner: Nathan Byrne (Head of Data Platforms) — nathan.byrne@clarityretail.com — he controls the platform budget and will need to sign off as economic buyer.
- Finance sponsor: Priya Shah (cc’d) will route the PO and handle net-30 terms.
- Legal timeline: expect 10–14 business days for our standard vendor review and DPA check.

If you can provide a PO-ready quote and the SOW template, we’ll route internally. Happy to do a 20-min follow-up with Nathan if helpful (he’s in-market on Wed afternoon).

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Huang | Director, AI Platforms
Clarity Retail
alex.huang@clarityretail.com | +1 (212) 555-0133

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial path & approver roster for Redwood trial (internal)

Thanks for the heads up — copied the thread into our procurement playbook. Notes and recommended commercial paths: 

1) If they can do a card-start: propose a 30-day trial with a capped spend ($7,500) to reduce procurement friction. Create invoice for immediate charge and convert to PO if they decide to expand.

2) If they prefer PO/SOW: prepare a minimal SOW (scope + acceptance + trial metrics) and our standard MSA + DPA. Legal will need to own the redline window; expect 10 business days baseline.

3) Marketplace option: publishing to AWS Marketplace takes ~2 weeks to onboard but it streamlines procurement long-term. If Alex confirms marketplace preference, we should prioritize starting the AWS listing simultaneously with legal review.

Internal asks for Jordan:
- Send Nathan Byrne’s contact into the thread and request a short intro call (15–20 min) — we need clarity on committed spend and signatory authority.
- Attach a PO-ready quote and the SOW template we can pre-populate. I’m attaching Redwood-SOW-template.pdf to this internal note.

If they route via PO: Ben, be prepared to review any discount request or non-standard payment terms.

-Marissa

Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Alex / Priya / Nathan — thanks, appreciate the quick answers. Nathan — welcome to the thread.

I’ve attached a PO-ready quote (Redwood-trial-quote.pdf) and a short SOW template (Redwood-SOW-template.pdf) Marissa mentioned. Two suggested paths so you can pick what fits procurement:

Path A (fast): corporate card, capped $7.5k charge to validate ops and perf within 48 hours. No SOW required. We can convert to PO after successful validation.
Path B (formal): PO + signed SOW, pilot starts after signature; expect ~10 business day legal review.

Action items:
- Nathan: can you confirm you are the economic buyer for this pilot and whether you would sign a PO or need an MSA + SOW to be present? (Please confirm name and signatory email.)
- Priya: once Nathan confirms, can you advise on required PO fields and preferred invoice cadence?
- Alex: let us know if Redwood should initiate AWS Marketplace onboarding in parallel. That could shorten procurement friction long-term.

I’ll schedule a 20-min intro with Nathan for Wed 29 Jun 2027 2:00pm PT — if that doesn’t work, please propose an alternate.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
